input.question: What are the mailing street address and name of the school with the seventh-highest recorded average mathematics score?

cases.oracle: SELECT sc.MailStreet, sc.School FROM satscores AS sat JOIN schools AS sc ON sc.CDSCode = sat.cds WHERE sat.rtype = 'S' AND sat.AvgScrMath IS NOT NULL ORDER BY sat.AvgScrMath DESC, sat.cds LIMIT 1 OFFSET 6

input.question: What is the Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12) in the school administered by an administrator whose first name is Alusine. List the district code of the school.
input.evidence: K-12 free-meal eligibility percentage is K-12 free-meal recipients divided by K-12 enrollment, times 100.

cases.oracle: SELECT T1.`Free Meal Count (K-12)` * 100 / T1.`Enrollment (K-12)`, T1.`District Code` FROM frpm AS T1 INNER JOIN schools AS T2 ON T1.CDSCode = T2.CDSCode WHERE T2.AdmFName1 = 'Alusine'

input.question: A parent is asking about a school and could only give me the CDS code 1612590137943. Can you look up that school and give me its name, county, district, and city; its K-12 enrollment; the number of K-12 students eligible for free or reduced price meals and the percentage eligible (report the percentage exactly as it appears, without rounding); and the SAT results - number of test takers, average reading score, average math score, average writing score, and the number of test takers whose total score is at least 1500?
input.evidence: CDS code: the state's County-District-School identification code assigned to each school; FRPM: the Free or Reduced Price Meal program, where the FRPM count is the number of students eligible.

cases.oracle: SELECT s.School AS school_name, s.County AS county, s.District AS district, s.City AS city, f.`Enrollment (K-12)` AS enrollment_k12, f.`FRPM Count (K-12)` AS frpm_count, f.`Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)` AS pct_eligible_frpm, sat.NumTstTakr AS num_sat_takers, sat.AvgScrRead AS avg_reading, sat.AvgScrMath AS avg_math, sat.AvgScrWrite AS avg_writing, sat.NumGE1500 AS num_ge_1500 FROM schools s JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode LEFT JOIN satscores sat ON sat.cds = s.CDSCode WHERE CAST(s.CDSCode AS INTEGER) = 1612590137943

input.question: What is the ratio of merged Unified School District schools in Orange County to merged Elementary School District schools?

cases.oracle: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN DOC = 54 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN DOC = 52 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM schools WHERE StatusType = 'Merged' AND County = 'Orange'

input.question: What note was recorded for the fundraising proceeds received on September 14, 2019?

cases.oracle: SELECT notes FROM income WHERE source = 'Fundraising' AND date_received = '2019-09-14'

input.question: List the name of students that have attended more than 7 events.

cases.oracle: SELECT T1.first_name, T1.last_name FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN attendance AS T2 ON T1.member_id = T2.link_to_member GROUP BY T2.link_to_member HAVING COUNT(T2.link_to_event) > 7

input.question: Our officer team wants to settle a debate about whether we pull more weight than the rest of the club, so we need the attendance numbers before the next meeting. Could you tell us two things: the average number of events attended per officer, and the average number of events attended per other student, each rounded to two decimal places? To be clear on who counts where: officers are the members holding the position of President, Vice President, Secretary, or Treasurer, and everyone else in the club counts as an other student. Each average should cover every member of its group, and include every event in the club's records - there's no date cutoff.

cases.oracle: WITH t AS (SELECT m.member_id, m.position, COUNT(a.link_to_event) AS cnt FROM member m LEFT JOIN attendance a ON a.link_to_member = m.member_id GROUP BY m.member_id, m.position) SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN t.position IN ('President','Vice President','Secretary','Treasurer') THEN t.cnt END), 2) AS officer_avg, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN t.position NOT IN ('President','Vice President','Secretary','Treasurer') THEN t.cnt END), 2) AS other_students_avg FROM t

input.question: Which closed events are tied for the highest ratio of total spending to total budget amount?

cases.oracle: WITH ratios AS ( SELECT e.event_id, e.event_name, CAST(SUM(b.spent) AS DECIMAL(20,4)) / NULLIF(SUM(b.amount), 0) AS ratio FROM event AS e JOIN budget AS b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE e.status = 'Closed' GROUP BY e.event_id, e.event_name HAVING SUM(b.amount) > 0 ) SELECT event_name FROM ratios WHERE ratio = (SELECT MAX(ratio) FROM ratios)

input.question: How many distinct patients have at least one positive CRP laboratory result and no recorded patient description?

cases.oracle: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE l.CRP LIKE '%+' AND p.Description IS NULL

input.question: I'm screening outpatient clinic patients with anemia for rheumatologic autoimmunity. Among patients who were followed as outpatients (rather than admitted to the hospital) and who ever had a hemoglobin value below 10 on any lab test, who showed the strongest anti-ribonuclear protein antibody response? Please return, for every patient whose anti-ribonuclear protein antibody level reached the highest point ever recorded on their lab tests (list all of them if several share that highest level): the patient ID, the patient's sex, and that highest-ever recorded anti-ribonuclear protein antibody level. Nothing else.
input.evidence: Anti-ribonuclear protein refers to the antibody measured in the laboratory tests (anti-RNP).

cases.oracle: SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, MAX(CAST(r.RNP AS REAL)) AS highest_level FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory r ON r.ID = p.ID WHERE p.Admission = '-' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory h WHERE h.ID = p.ID AND h.HGB < 10) GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX HAVING MAX(CAST(r.RNP AS REAL)) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(r2.RNP AS REAL)) FROM Patient p2 JOIN Laboratory r2 ON r2.ID = p2.ID WHERE p2.Admission = '-' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory h2 WHERE h2.ID = p2.ID AND h2.HGB < 10))

input.question: Across laboratory records with PLT > 400 for female patients whose patient profile lists an SLE diagnosis, what is the average ALB value rounded to four decimal places?

cases.oracle: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CAST(l.ALB AS DECIMAL(10, 4))), 4) FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE l.PLT > 400 AND ((',' || REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(COALESCE(p.Diagnosis, ''), CHAR(13), ','), CHAR(10), ','), CHAR(29), ','), CHAR(11), ','), '  ', ','), ' ', '') || ',') LIKE '%,SLE,%' OR (',' || REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(COALESCE(p.Diagnosis, ''), CHAR(13), ','), CHAR(10), ','), CHAR(29), ','), CHAR(11), ','), '  ', ','), ' ', '') || ',') LIKE '%,SLE(%') AND p.SEX = 'F'

input.question: What was the average age of the register's patients in 1999, considering all patients who ever had marked or worse proteinuria on a lab test? Age in 1999 means 1999 minus the patient's year of birth. Marked or worse proteinuria means grade 3 or 4 on the original scale, or 300, 1000 or above on the scale used since 1987; traces and grades 1 and 2 don't count. I just need the one average number, in years.
input.evidence: U-PRO = proteinuria result of a laboratory test; TR = traces of proteinuria.

cases.oracle: SELECT AVG('1999' - CAST(STRFTIME('%Y', Birthday) AS INTEGER)) AS average_age FROM Patient WHERE ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` IN ('3','4') OR CAST(REPLACE(`U-PRO`, '>=', '') AS REAL) >= 300)

input.question: Among molecules containing at least one single bond, what is the average number of oxygen atoms per molecule? Include molecules with no oxygen and round to four decimal places.
input.evidence: The '-' bond-type symbol denotes a single bond.

cases.oracle: WITH molecules AS ( SELECT DISTINCT molecule_id FROM bond WHERE bond_type = '-' ), oxygen AS ( SELECT molecule_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM atom WHERE element = 'o' GROUP BY molecule_id ) SELECT ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(oxygen.n, 0)), 4) FROM molecules LEFT JOIN oxygen ON oxygen.molecule_id = molecules.molecule_id

input.question: For the molecule containing atom TR041_10, I'd like to know the molecule id, whether it's carcinogenic (YES or NO), and the number of multiple bonds in that molecule. Please use the rule that a molecule labeled '+' is carcinogenic (YES) and one labeled '-' is not (NO).

cases.oracle: SELECT T2.molecule_id, IIF(T2.label = '+', 'YES', 'NO') AS flag_carcinogenic, COUNT(T3.bond_id) AS multiple_bonds FROM atom AS T1 INNER JOIN molecule AS T2 ON T1.molecule_id = T2.molecule_id INNER JOIN bond AS T3 ON T3.molecule_id = T2.molecule_id WHERE T1.atom_id = 'TR041_10' AND T3.bond_type <> '-' GROUP BY T2.molecule_id, T2.label

input.question: How many atoms occur in molecules that have at least one triple bond and at least one phosphorus or bromine atom?
input.evidence: The '#' bond-type symbol denotes a triple bond.

cases.oracle: WITH triple AS (SELECT DISTINCT molecule_id FROM bond WHERE bond_type = '#'), hetero AS (SELECT DISTINCT molecule_id FROM atom WHERE element IN ('p', 'br')), qualified AS (SELECT t.molecule_id FROM triple AS t JOIN hetero AS h ON h.molecule_id = t.molecule_id) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM atom AS a JOIN qualified AS q ON q.molecule_id = a.molecule_id

input.question: I'm building a control group of nitrogen-containing structures for a carcinogenicity review. How many molecules in the database contain at least one nitrogen atom, where none of those nitrogen atoms takes part in a double bond or a triple bond? A nitrogen held only by single bonds is fine; any nitrogen in a double or triple bond disqualifies the molecule. Molecules with no nitrogen at all don't count. I just need the single number of such molecules.
input.evidence: Nitrogen refers to the element code 'n'; '=' denotes a double bond; '#' denotes a triple bond; '-' denotes a single bond.

cases.oracle: SELECT COUNT(*) AS number_of_molecules FROM molecule AS m WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM atom AS a WHERE a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND a.element = 'n') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM atom AS a2 INNER JOIN connected AS c ON c.atom_id = a2.atom_id OR c.atom_id2 = a2.atom_id INNER JOIN bond AS b ON b.bond_id = c.bond_id WHERE a2.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND a2.element = 'n' AND b.bond_type <> '-')

input.question: What known full names belong to superheroes tied for the highest strength attribute value?

cases.oracle: SELECT DISTINCT s.full_name FROM superhero AS s JOIN hero_attribute AS ha ON ha.hero_id = s.id JOIN attribute AS a ON a.id = ha.attribute_id WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Strength' AND ha.attribute_value = ( SELECT MAX(ha2.attribute_value) FROM hero_attribute AS ha2 JOIN attribute AS a2 ON a2.id = ha2.attribute_id WHERE a2.attribute_name = 'Strength' ) AND s.full_name IS NOT NULL AND s.full_name <> '-' ORDER BY s.full_name ASC

input.question: I'm writing an article about heroes who fall outside the classic good-versus-evil divide. How many superheroes in the database have an alignment that is neither good nor bad? Please give me just that count. Note that this should cover all superheroes in the database.
input.evidence: good: a superhero whose alignment is Good; bad: a superhero whose alignment is Bad; alignment: the moral category assigned to a superhero

cases.oracle: SELECT COUNT(*) AS neither_good_nor_bad FROM superhero AS s LEFT JOIN alignment AS a ON s.alignment_id = a.id WHERE a.alignment IS NULL OR a.alignment NOT IN ('Good', 'Bad')

input.question: Among superheroes from 170 through 190 cm tall whose recorded eye-colour category is unknown, list their names.

cases.oracle: SELECT DISTINCT T1.superhero_name FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN colour AS T2 ON T1.eye_colour_id = T2.id WHERE T1.height_cm BETWEEN 170 AND 190 AND T2.colour = 'No Colour'

input.question: I'm researching heroes like A-Bomb. What is the average height in centimetres of the superheroes in A-Bomb's group? Please give me just that single number, rounded to one decimal place. Note that A-Bomb itself belongs to its group and should be included, and only heroes whose height is actually on record should count toward the average-anyone without a recorded height should be left out rather than counted as some height.
input.evidence: In this request, "group" refers to race.

cases.oracle: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN height_cm > 0 THEN height_cm END), 1) AS average_height_cm FROM superhero WHERE race_id = (SELECT race_id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name = 'A-Bomb')
